headline: DNA is life's instruction manual—information that tells cells what to build and how
universal_truth: Instructions persist better than artifacts; pass on the recipe, not just the dish
fun_facts: If you unraveled all the DNA in your body, it would stretch to the sun and back 600 times
You share 60% of your DNA with bananas—life uses the same basic code
DNA contains only four 'letters' (A, T, C, G) but encodes everything about you
discussion_questions: What 'code' runs your life—beliefs, habits, values?
How is information passed down in your family or organization?
What instructions have you inherited that you didn't choose?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You started as a single cell, yet that cell knew how to become you—every organ, every protein, every detail. How? DNA. It's the instruction manual: information that tells life what to build. Just four letters, encoding everything.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: DNA is information that builds bodies. This idea—that life is information—has profound implications. What does it teach us?
cliff.prompt: What does life as information mean?

options.text: Life is ultimately about information transfer—what persists across generations is instructions, not bodies; the recipe outlasts any single dish
options.response: Yes. Your body will die, but your DNA pattern could continue for millions of years. Information is more durable than matter. The code persists; instances come and go.

options.text: DNA is just a molecule in cells
options.response: It's a molecule, but what makes it special is that it carries information...

q1.title: Four Letters, Infinite Combinations
q1.script: DNA has only four letters: A, T, C, G. Yet their combinations encode every living thing. Simple rules, combined creatively, produce infinite complexity. Constraint enables rather than limits.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Four Letters, Infinite Combinations"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Instructions vs Artifacts
q2.script: DNA doesn't store a miniature human—it stores instructions for building one. The recipe, not the dish. Instructions are compact, copyable, and can build fresh instances indefinitely.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Your Inherited Code
q3.script: You run on code you didn't write—genetic, cultural, familial. Understanding your inherited instructions helps you see what's truly you and what you might consciously revise.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Instructions persist better than artifacts. Pass on the recipe, not just the dish. Think in terms of information that can replicate.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 264. Tomorrow, we'll explore what you get from parents—heredity. Until then, consider what instructions run your life.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Code Audit - What Instructions Run You?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify inherited and chosen operating instructions
growTrack.activity: What 'code' runs your life—beliefs, assumptions, habits, values? Which did you inherit versus consciously choose? Understanding your programming is the first step to debugging or upgrading it.
